purpose: Separate human-supervised cortex agents from autonomous organic agents so lifecycle, MCP refresh, repo mutation and operator review are routed through the correct control boundary.
invariants: Human-supervised cortex sessions may rewrite DNA directly only after coordination claims are held.
Autonomous agents must not rewrite DNA directly from inference output; they produce proposals, tasks, patches or observations behind an executor boundary.
MCP exposure is a projection of organism capabilities, not a hand-maintained cortex preference list.
Capability changes may trigger autonomous mcp-reload planning, but public/operator-visible effects still require proof and review according to risk.
Repo-affecting autonomous work requires declared targets before execution starts.
The same model provider can appear in different autonomy classes depending on transport and supervision.

autonomy_classes.promotion_rule: Results return to the supervising cortex or operator proposal queue before public/deploy promotion.
Produces agent proposals, lifecycle tasks, observations or patch artifacts; operator/runtime gates decide promotion.
Executes approved or registry-authorized work and emits proofs; it does not invent product intent.

mcp_freshness_autonomy.trigger: REST/MCP/API/exposure contract changes detected from DNA or runtime freshness probes
forbidden_actions: compile MCP on an interactive cortex as canonical release
edit infra/agent-exposure.json without declared targets and claims
publish new public capabilities without operator review

routing_rule: When a request can be handled by either a human-supervised cortex or an autonomous organ agent, route deterministic lifecycle maintenance to the autonomous organ agent and reserve cortex attention for DNA changes, ambiguous design decisions, policy exceptions and operator review.
